Rzeszow New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rzeszów, Poland

Not demolished. Rzeszów's New Cemetery was established in 1849 southeast of the market square and enlarged several times to a final 2.5 hectares. From 1940, the Germans systematically destroyed the site, taking valuable tombstones for sale and using sandstone ones for construction, some moved to a nearby brickyard; hundreds of ghetto victims were executed and buried in mass graves whose locations have never been identified. After the war, survivors recovered several hundred tombstones, though some were later stolen again; a Holocaust memorial was erected in 1947, and three ohels were built between 1981 and 1988 over the graves of six rabbis and tzadiks. Today the cemetery holds over 750 tomb enclosures and around 650 tombstones and fragments, the oldest dating to 1849, with inscriptions in both German and Polish reflecting the region's shifting rule.
